meta.title: Ondra Load Self-Check
meta.description: Ten load checks that only judge and never block startup. What they verify is not whether the code is correct but whether the package was actually mounted. The handbook names three silent failures that raise nothing, break nothing visible, and leave no trace in the UI: a manifest without the bundle patch declaration makes the host print one line to stderr and never load the package; a wrong patch semantic makes the host warn once and skip the row; an entry field or a name that disagrees with the package name is equally silent. All three look the same afterwards: a clean log, a healthy process, and a feature that is not there. So the tenth check ports the host's patch composition, computes the entry tree the host would actually see, and looks for itself inside it. The port follows the source rather than the summary: the name mismatch check only applies to rows without insert, the insert branch never looks at the name, an insert into a group whose config is not an array silently replaces it with an empty array, and inserted rows are indexed immediately so a later patch in the same list can target them. Missing any of these makes the check report a failure on a package that actually loads. Syntax the subset parser does not support is reported as unverifiable rather than as a pass, because a check that says loadable while the host says otherwise is worse than no check. The first nine are mechanical: structure, manifest, compiler config, entry contract, unique service keys, resolvable dependencies, no cross-package imports, degradation in place, and complete deliverables. Degradation is heuristic and never fatal; key uniqueness and dependency resolution need a repository-wide index and say so honestly when the index is empty instead of treating a single package as unique. The scan root defaults to empty, because a guessed root makes the check pass against the wrong directory, which is worse than not checking.
